newsitem.title: UK: London silver ticks slightly higher, gold steady.
newsitem.headline: London silver ticks slightly higher, gold steady.

text.p: Silver perked up on Thursday afternoon after teetering just above a key price support level, but gold resisted the temptation to follow it much higher.
"There's been a bit of buying in silver since New York opened and gold came up a bit on the back of it," a dealer said.
"Silver was pretty cheap down there and dealers have been buying it up," she said.
Silver pushed up about five cents from its weak opening level, and was trading at $4.86/$4.88 an ounce.
Gold also came off its lows of the day, but fixed little changed at $379.50 an ounce, compared to $379.30 in the morning.
Platinum and palladium also edged slightly higher with stronger silver.
If silver decisively broke above the $4.86 resistance level it had the potential to head above $4.90, although the key $5.00 level was probably out of reach for now, dealers said.
But gold, balancing precariously on the $379-$380 support level, showed less scope on the upside in the near term after slumping some $3.00 this week, they added.
"There was some producer selling overnight and there's more fund and producer selling just above," a dealer said, pegging the top of its range at around $381 an ounce.
On the downside, gold may yet target support at $377.50 and then $375.00 if recent selling pressure continued, dealers said.
"Sentiment remains quite negative and technically it looks pretty bad, but up till now prices have remained within range," a dealer said.
The market's mood has soured since gold's attempt to break out of a medium-term downtrend failed last week.
A lack of investor interest in precious metals and recent bearish talk of possible European central bank sales of gold reserves had further depressed the market, analysts said.
But some dealers dismissed such sales as an important near term factor, as they had already been factored into the price.
The effect of reported gold sales by producers in South Africa and Australia were also sparking disparate views.
"There hasn't been a noticeable increase in producer selling. That's clear because we're still in the old price range," a dealer said.
Platinum and palladium, although slightly firmer, were still vulnerable to the downside.
Platinum was indicated up $1.30 at $381.80/$382.80 an ounce, while palladium was $1.00 firmer at $116.50/$117.50.
